current_focus: Extended the Phase D lane with full-system release witnesses that build generated .tboot/.tdisk artifacts, validate release manifest and disk metadata, boot them through TosRuntime diagnostics/reset, prove visible boot framebuffer plus queued host input behavior, drive the OS 3 secure login into the desktop launcher, and exercise bundled apps. The Settings persistence witness saves an explicit brightness change to /etc/os3.cfg on the mutable .tdisk and reads it back visibly after reset. The Terminal slice launches through the release desktop, verifies Terminal execs Shell, and proves blocked raw-input wake/delivery. The reboot command now crosses a real privileged power boundary: /bin/reboot invokes sys_reboot 58, the kernel raises power_control after aggregate system-capability authorization, and TosRuntime cold-loads the same release image while preserving the attached mutable disk. The crash slice adds /bin/crash and proves a typed Shell command can fault with a routed divide-by-zero, leave pid 106 inspectable as PROC_CRASHED with exit_status 6, keep the VM running without a guest reboot, and expose durable crashed_* fields in crash_report.txt. The app-bundle/VFS slice extends TinyFS past the old direct-plus-one-indirect-block ceiling with chained indirect index blocks, then proves a real compiled /bin/calculator GUI executable installs through OSKernel, launches through ConsumerShell/sysExec, and still execs after disk-image reboot/remount. The desktop-shell app slice adds deterministic draw-contract checks for About, Help, Text Editor, and Task Manager so those apps are covered beyond marker-only standalone smoke. The latest full-system release slice adds Task Manager, Paint, and File Manager product-path witnesses: desktop hotkey 2 increments the /bin/task_manager app-registry row and paints the visible SYSTEM TASKS dashboard columns, hotkey 3 increments /bin/paint and drives graphics-mode mouse drawing into the raw framebuffer, and hotkey 4 increments the /bin/file_manager row and paints the live root VFS browser.

improvement_signals.summary: tests_next/README.md, AGENTS.md, and INDEX.md now direct future agents to record optimization and improvement opportunities when deterministic tests expose them.

Vector runtime tests now pin lane-mode conversions, VPERMUTE/VBLEND selection, indexed memory side effects, reductions, and lane-local fault masks so future vector optimizations can be compared safely.
Native TCL assembler parity tests compile and run the TCL harness per fixture; future harness caching could reduce tests_next_fast time once parity behavior remains pinned.
Per-core snapshot tests now pin MMU CSR, vector lane/fault, accumulator, syscall, console, GPU, and block-device staging state so scheduler or core-state optimizations can be validated safely.

Compiler pipeline tests now distinguish pure match lowering, which can execute branch-free through TSEL, from side-effectful match lowering, which must preserve conditional branch structure and selected-arm syscall behavior.

Compiler optimizer/allocation tests now pin constant-folding, CSE, branch simplification, spill pressure, interference graph, and move-coalescing counters so future optimizer changes can report improvements without losing correctness evidence.

Native parser and ulib integration tests compile larger Trit sources, so they are wired through next_compiler_native_ulib and tests_next_compiler_full rather than tests_next_fast; future module caching or incremental compilation can target this cost boundary.

Phase C.5 bootstrap golden tests now compare OptimizationLevel::None and OptimizationLevel::Basic VM output for arithmetic, recursion, aggregate, atomic, pointer-state, and ulib_mini programs so optimizer changes have deterministic semantic guardrails.

Phase D facade tests now pin block CSR persistence, TinyFS direct/indirect extents, reboot remounts, process image handoff, capability gates, IPC queue consumption, and kill/wait cleanup so future VFS, scheduler, and kernel-resource optimizations have deterministic behavior checks.

The native Phase D wait driver now pins TLB miss/hit and span-cache hit counters around futex validation, plus blocked-to-runnable transitions for futex, sleep, IPC, and wait_event paths, giving future scheduler and translation-cache optimizations concrete correctness boundaries.

The native process-control cleanup driver now pins denied cross-process control, process-capability/self-control paths, fd/window/IPC/wait/PTE cleanup, zombie getproc metadata, orphan handling, and waitpid reaping so future resource-cleanup or process-table optimizations can be checked against deterministic state.

The VFS recovery slice now pins journal commit boundaries, rescue-root boot recovery, disk-backed executable metadata/payload reboot, signed package sidecars, and release/package manifest markers so future persistence and image-builder optimizations have deterministic failure-mode checks.

The runtime/SDK slice now pins sbrk heap-base progression, allocator free-list reuse, parse/string helpers, public SDK syscall lowering, and widget dead-strip/behavior so future runtime, SDK, and app-toolkit optimizations can be checked against focused witnesses.

The drivers/HAL slice now pins device-tree validation diagnostics, console/timer/input/GPU CSR behavior, block CSR read-only/error/flush boundaries, and kernel/hal.trit DTB plus framebuffer descriptor runtime behavior so future driver, HAL, and device-state optimizations have deterministic contract checks.

The graphics/GUI slice now pins host text/graphics framebuffer revision behavior, native compositor dirty clearing, z-order occlusion, resize redraw, close/key/mouse routing, and widget dirty/text redraw paths so future rendering, input, and widget optimizations can be checked against deterministic snapshots and VM-visible state.

The apps/consumer bundle slice now pins APP_MANIFEST-to-release-builder alignment, GUI registry coverage, GUI app marker/framebuffer/GPU outputs, shared CLI/service alias link options, compiled calculator release VFS image installation, and consumer shell boot/login/app/file/crash/preference reboot persistence.
APP_MANIFEST GUI stack_words had drifted from build_tos_image.cpp and test_all_apps release options; GUI entries now record the 1024-word release stack hint and tests enforce that alignment.

apps.shell.indirect_cli_executable_handoff first proved a real compiled /bin/sync image larger than the direct-block TinyFS window could install through OSKernel and launch through ConsumerShell/sysExec. vfs.tinyfs.chained_indirect_extent_reboot and apps.shell.gui_sized_executable_handoff now extend the facade to chained TinyFS indirect index blocks, so a real compiled /bin/calculator GUI executable larger than the old one-indirect-block capacity installs, launches, preserves payload/header metadata, and execs again after disk-image reboot/remount.

TinyFS now chains indirect index blocks by using the final index word as a backward-compatible continuation pointer when needed. The new VFS witness writes beyond the old direct-plus-one-index ceiling, runs consistency checks before and after remount, and proves full payload preservation.

The desktop shell slice now pins remaining GUI app standalone markers, deterministic draw contracts for About, Help, Text Editor, and Task Manager framebuffer cells, failed-launch child/window cleanup, taskbar ordering, focus handoff, not-responding suspension and force-close behavior, crash dialog/log persistence, and custom registry capability metadata.

apps.bundle.remaining_gui_draw_contracts renames each app main inside the test harness and calls real app drawing helpers directly. It verifies About identity/status cells, Help shortcut guidance, Text Editor document/newline/cursor layout, and Task Manager process-state labels, giving future app UI changes a more useful signal than marker-only standalone smoke.

The full-system release slice now builds generated .tboot/.tdisk artifacts, validates manifest and native-VFS metadata, boots through TosRuntime diagnostics, drives login and bundled apps, proves Settings persistence, launches Task Manager, Paint, and File Manager through desktop hotkey/app-registry paths, and exercises Terminal -> Shell -> typed reboot end to end. The reboot witness observes exactly one guest cold-reset generation, the same boot image and mutable disk, cleared cycle/log/process/app state, and a successful second login/desktop boot.

full_system.release.task_manager_launch_screen proves the release desktop hotkey launches /bin/task_manager and paints the visible SYSTEM TASKS dashboard columns. A stronger attempted assertion for the lower KILL/RUN/EXIT action row did not appear within an additional 2M release steps after the title/table became visible, so future Task Manager or os_ps/render-loop work has a focused latency/completeness target.

full_system.release.file_manager_launch_screen initially showed that the File Manager title/footer can become visible before the root os_readdir results have painted. The final witness waits for live / entries such as bin and apps, giving future File Manager, scheduler, and VFS/read-dir optimizations a concrete settle condition instead of accepting title-only launch evidence.

full_system.release.paint_launch_graphics_canvas proves the release desktop hotkey launches /bin/paint, switches TosRuntime into Graphics80x60 mode, publishes the yellow plus cursor sprite, routes host mouse input into the app, and mutates the raw graphics framebuffer. This gives future GPU, input, double-buffering, and app-loop optimizations a full-system correctness boundary.

full_system.release.rootfs_registry_decoding expands the generated sparse .tdisk into a 32768-block native VFS image and reads /apps/registry, /system/bin.manifest, and /apps/settings.app through the release native-VFS table layout, so productization metadata is checked as filesystem state rather than raw byte presence. The first attempt exposed that OSKernel::boot still targets the older TinyFileSystem facade, making native-VFS read helpers a useful future consolidation opportunity.

full_system.release.cli_command_descriptors proves /bin/shell, /bin/sh, /bin/sync, /bin/reboot, /bin/shutdown, and /bin/crash are present as v2 disk-backed executable descriptors with the expected release stack classes, bounded text ranges, and non-empty serialized text. This narrows command-flow gaps to runtime behavior rather than missing release-root command installation.

TosRuntime diagnostics now include app_registry.json with active kernel app-registry rows, inode ids, caps, trusted bits, versions, image limits, and launch counters. This makes release app-launch behavior observable without relying on guest.log output.

full_system.release.terminal_shell_reboot_command proves the release desktop launches Terminal, Terminal sys_execs /bin/shell, queued input wakes Shell, and typed reboot invokes /bin/reboot and sys_reboot. The VM runtime performs one cold reset, preserves the mutable disk, clears volatile guest state, exports reboot generation counters, and reaches a fresh desktop.

full_system.release.terminal_shell_crash_diagnostics proves the release desktop launches Terminal, Shell execs /bin/crash, and a routed divide-by-zero user trap becomes PROC_CRASHED pid 106 with exit_status 6 instead of taking down the VM or rebooting. crash_report.txt now includes boot generation, guest reboot count, and durable crashed_pid/crashed_parent_pid/crashed_exit_status fields.

Rerunning tests_next_fast exposed that a pending dirty VM change stopped timer countdown while routed code was in kernel privilege, breaking vm.timer.pending_defers_across_critical_section. recordCycle now counts enabled timers regardless of privilege while still routing only when interrupt_enable permits, restoring deferred timer IRQ behavior.

When Shell blocked in wait_event with every user context asleep or blocked, kernel_schedule_next entered costly tier reconciliation with interrupts disabled and could not reach a timer wake within the release step budget. The scheduler now detects an empty runnable set, services input/window/timeout work through kernel_timer_tick until a context wakes, and switches directly to it; the native Phase D scheduler helper checks and full_system.release.terminal_shell_reboot_command both pass.

The blocking Shell input conversion initially issued syscall 55 in standalone compiler/VM execution, where routed kernel traps are not installed and extended OS syscalls are unsupported. Shell now detects a nonzero trap vector before using blocking wait_event; release execution remains blocking, while the standalone production-layer witness consumes raw console CSR input and exits.

A release Settings persistence probe reached the desktop and accepted hotkey 5, then left pid 105 runnable at context_epc 1966 with the desktop still showing 'LAUNCH 5 ...' after roughly 12M additional steps and zero block-device writes. The root cause was Settings using unmapped 20000-series scratch buffers; the app now uses the mapped user scratch range and full_system.release.settings_launch_screen proves the visible launch without claiming release-visible Settings persistence.
Settings cfg_load now uses the Phase D sys_open mode 0 read-only contract instead of the create-if-missing mode 2 path, keeping first launch from creating /etc/os3.cfg before an explicit save.

The release Settings persistence witness exposed cfg_load and cfg_save treating valid fd 0 as failure. Settings now treats only negative sys_open results as errors, and full_system.release.settings_persistence_readback proves /etc/os3.cfg is saved, fsynced, present in sparse disk records, and read back visibly after TosRuntime reset.

Settings config, path, password, and event scratch buffers moved from 20000-20300 into the kernel-mapped user scratch window around 10000, resolving the release store-page-fault loop before first paint.

After the Settings persistence fix, grep found fd <= 0 checks in apps/sync.trit and apps/text_editor.trit. Those apps now treat only negative os_open results as failures, and apps.bundle.fd_zero_open_guards rejects the stale fd <= 0 idiom across bundled app sources.

Attempting to drive Terminal -> shell -> /bin/reboot showed that guest.log remains empty for this release terminal path, so full_system.release.terminal_launch_reset_diagnostics uses process_table.json and crash_report.txt as authoritative diagnostics, and full_system.release.terminal_shell_reboot_command now uses app_registry.json launch counters for command execution evidence.

The release login/app-launch witness needs multi-million-step waits to reach login and launch calculator, giving future boot, scheduler, app-loading, or host-runtime acceleration work a concrete correctness-preserving optimization target.

stage_tos_release exposed missing packaging/windows README and license-note inputs; those files now exist and stage_tos_release, smoke_tos_release, package_tos_release, and release image inspection pass.

A broader runtime fixture that executed ulib itoa/printf paths did not halt within the focused step budget, so current coverage keeps those helpers as compile/link witnesses and queues a dedicated runtime investigation instead of mixing it into the parse/string test.
